Comparative Genomic Analysis and Phylogenetic Relationships of Dengue Virus Serotypes Using R

2021/ICT/91

2026-11-11

1. Introduction

Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease caused by the dengue virus. It has four major serotypes: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4.

This project uses bioinformatics techniques in R to compare eight dengue virus nucleotide sequences and investigate their genetic similarities and differences.

2. Objectives

  • Analyze nucleotide frequencies.
  • Calculate GC content.
  • Compare genome lengths.
  • Perform multiple sequence alignment.
  • Calculate genetic distances.
  • Construct a phylogenetic tree.

3. Dataset Description

Eight nucleotide sequences were downloaded from the NCBI GenBank database.

Serotype Accession numbers
DENV-1 KM204119, EU848545
DENV-2 KM204118, AF038403
DENV-3 KU050695, M93130
DENV-4 KR011349, AY947539

4. Nucleotide Analysis

The nucleotide frequencies of adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G) and cytosine (C) were calculated.

5. Genome Length Comparison

The following graph compares the lengths of the eight dengue virus sequences.

6. GC Content Comparison

GC content represents the percentage of guanine and cytosine in each DNA sequence.

DENV-4 had the highest average GC content (47.21%), while DENV-2 had the lowest average GC content (46.05%).

7. Multiple Sequence Alignment

Multiple sequence alignment was performed using the DECIPHER package.

The aligned sequences are stored in:

results/aligned_dengue_sequences.fasta

This process helps compare corresponding nucleotide positions across the selected sequences.

8. Genetic Distance Analysis

Pairwise genetic distances were calculated using the raw distance model.

distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
  read.csv(
    "results/genetic_distance_matrix.csv",
    row.names = 1,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)

knitr::kable(round(distance_matrix, 5))

The two sequences within each serotype showed relatively low genetic distances.

9. Genetic Distance Heatmap

The heatmap visualizes the genetic distances between the eight sequences.

Lower genetic distances indicate greater sequence similarity, while higher values indicate greater differences.

10. Phylogenetic Tree

A Neighbor-Joining phylogenetic tree was constructed using the genetic distance matrix.

The two selected sequences belonging to each serotype formed a pair in the resulting tree.

11. Discussion

The analysis identified differences in nucleotide composition and GC content among the selected dengue virus sequences.

The genetic distance matrix showed that the two selected sequences within each serotype were more similar to each other than to sequences from different serotypes.

The phylogenetic tree supported these observations by grouping the two selected sequences belonging to each serotype together.

These findings describe the eight selected sequences and do not represent the complete genetic diversity of all dengue virus strains.

12. Limitations

  • Only eight sequences were included.
  • Two sequences represented each serotype.
  • The selected records have slightly different sequence lengths.
  • The raw distance model does not correct for multiple substitutions.
  • Bootstrap support was not calculated for the phylogenetic tree.

13. Conclusion

This project demonstrated the application of R-based bioinformatics techniques to comparative genomic analysis of dengue virus sequences.

Nucleotide frequency analysis, GC-content calculation, multiple sequence alignment, genetic distance calculation and phylogenetic tree construction were successfully performed.

The results showed genetic similarities between the selected sequences within each serotype and differences between the selected serotypes.
